title: The year of the elephant
hook: an army with an elephant marches on the Ka'ba and is turned back, in the year the Prophet ﷺ is born

segments.voice: Yesterday, Mecca: a dry valley, a trading tribe, and the House of Ibrahim ringed with idols. Your line was a house waiting. What in your life is waiting? Day seventy-nine.

Imagine you're a shepherd outside Mecca, and over the southern hills comes an army. Soldiers, banners, dust. And in front of them, something nobody in the valley has ever seen: an elephant. A living mountain, walking. The army has come for one reason: to tear down the Ka'ba. Its commander, a man named Abraha, governor of Yemen, had built a grand house of worship in his own city, and he wanted the pilgrims of Arabia to go there instead. So he's come to knock down the competition. The Meccans are traders, not soldiers. They look at the elephant, and they head for the hills.
screen: `AN ARMY FROM THE SOUTH.` → `IN FRONT: AN ELEPHANT.` → `THE MECCANS HEAD FOR THE HILLS.`

segments.voice: The early biography of the Prophet, by Ibn Ishaq, tells what happened next. Abraha's soldiers seize two hundred camels belonging to the chief of Mecca, an old man named 'Abd al-Muttalib. So 'Abd al-Muttalib goes to meet Abraha, and Abraha is impressed: a dignified man. Surely he's come to plead for the Ka'ba. But 'Abd al-Muttalib asks only for his camels. Abraha is disappointed. You came about camels, and not the house of your fathers' religion? And the old man answers, in the words the story remembers: I am the owner of the camels. The House has its own Lord, who will protect it. Then the elephant, the story says, kneels down facing Mecca and will not get up. Turn it toward Yemen, it walks. Turn it toward the Ka'ba, it sits. And the Qur'an tells the rest in a short surah, the hundred and fifth, called Al-Fil, the Elephant. In Pickthall's translation it begins: “Hast thou not seen how thy Lord dealt with the owners of the Elephant?” Allah sent against them, it says, “swarms of flying creatures,” pelting them with stones of baked clay, until they were like chewed-up straw. The army is broken, and the House stands. The Arabs began counting years from it: the Year of the Elephant. And in that same year, around five hundred and seventy by the common reckoning, a boy was born in Mecca into 'Abd al-Muttalib's own family. His grandson. His name was Muhammad ﷺ. Muslims have long seen the timing as a sign: the House is protected, and the one who will restore it to the worship of One God is born.
screen: `ONLY THE CAMELS, PLEASE.` · `THE ELEPHANT KNEELS.` · `SWARMS OF FLYING CREATURES.` · `THE YEAR A BOY IS BORN.` · then, large: `THE HOUSE HAS AN OWNER.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: stand under the sky for one breath. If you can, step outside, or go to a window and look up. Take one long breath in, and let it out slowly. Notice how big it is up there, and how small the things that frighten you look against it. Then sit, wherever you are, and let the rest of the time be quiet. You don't have to protect everything yourself. If you pray, you can hand one worry to the Lord of the House. The bell holds the time.
The year of the elephant. The year an army came to destroy the Ka'ba and was turned back, and the year the Prophet ﷺ was born.
screen: `THE YEAR OF THE ELEPHANT — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: the house has an owner. Today, when you're tempted to carry something that isn't yours to carry, say it, and set it down. Tomorrow, the boy grows up an orphan. Day seventy-nine.

screen: `DAY 79 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: AN ORPHAN IN THE DESERT.`

howItsDone: Surah Al-Fil is one of the short surahs many Muslims learn as children and recite in prayer; the Year of the Elephant is remembered as the year of the Prophet's birth.

fork.setup: you're 'Abd al-Muttalib, chief of Mecca. an army with an elephant has seized your camels and come to destroy the Ka'ba. you meet its commander. what do you ask for?

original.note: Arabic: the elephant; the name of Surah 105.

trapdoor: what you thought: a strange old story about an elephant.
what it means: a proud army comes to destroy the House, the townspeople can't defend it, and it is defended anyway.

what a scholar hears: Arabs dated years by great events, and 'am al-fil, the Year of the Elephant, became the marker for the Prophet's birth; modern historians debate the exact year of Abraha's campaign.

sources.quoted: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord dealt with the owners of the Elephant?

sources.ref: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (Abraha, 'Abd al-Muttalib and the camels, the kneeling elephant)
sources.work: Sirat Rasul Allah (Ibn Ishaq, via Ibn Hisham)

notes: Pickthall 105:1 and 105:3 quoted from memory; confirm exact wording.
The camels, the kneeling elephant and 'Abd al-Muttalib's reply come from Ibn Ishaq's seerah, not the Qur'an; the script attributes them. Number of camels (200) per Ibn Ishaq; confirm.

Abraha is described neutrally as governor of Yemen who built a 'grand house of worship' (al-Qullays, a church, in San'a); the script avoids naming its religion to keep the story from reading as one faith against another. Confirm.
'Like chewed-up straw' paraphrases 105:5 (Pickthall: 'like green crops devoured'); confirm.
Date: the conventional 570; modern scholarship dates Abraha's campaign earlier (c. 552). The trapdoor notes the debate. Confirm.
